text: What is a high ankle sprain? Miami WR Malachi Toney's injury, Nov. 2026. A high ankle sprain is an injury to the ligaments that join the two lower leg bones above the ankle joint, rather than the ligaments on the outer side of the ankle. Miami Hurricanes receiver Malachi Toney has one, and sources say he will have surgery.. Miami Hurricanes receiver Malachi Toney is having surgery for a high ankle sprain, a development reported in early November 2026 that puts his return for the College Football Playoff in question.. Toney, a sophomore wide receiver, suffered the injury in practice during the week of Nov. 7, 2026, before Miami's game at No. 11 Notre Dame. Sources tell CBS Sports that the early estimate has him sidelined four to six weeks after ankle surgery, which would rule him out for the rest of the regular season. Before the injury, Toney led the ACC in receptions with 73, receiving yards with 1,027 and receiving touchdowns with 13. Miami's offense also depends on quarterback Darian Mensah, who had 25 touchdown passes and one interception at that point, and on Duke transfer Cooper Barkate, the most likely replacement for Toney's output. The Hurricanes hope Toney returns before the postseason. The College Football Playoff first round begins Dec. 18, and a top-four seed with a first-round bye would not play until Dec. 30 at the earliest, so a six-week recovery would still leave time for the playoffs.
